reason: The 2026-10-10 backfill covers were a shared explainer template (label, three numbered boxes, arrows, footer disclaimer). This revision replaces them with either a capture of the project's own output or a single mark drawn from what the project does.

covers.source: Godot web export in Slaymish/PlatformerGame (HTML/Assignment-1-godot.html) run headless in Chrome and captured at 2x. Title screen, untouched.
covers.alt: Title screen of Cookie Cat: hand-drawn lettering over a dark forest scene, from the game's own web export.

covers.source: Plotted from outputs/reference/nietzsche-profile.json in Slaymish/personal-language-corpus. Script: corpus-register-cover.py.
covers.alt: Scatter plot of 24 Nietzsche works: mean sentence length against exclamations per 1,000 words. Zarathustra and Poems and Dithyrambs sit short and exclamatory, Birth of Tragedy long and plain.
A grid of stat cells with one player's row picked out in red.
A wireframe solid with one red vertex, standing for the VRML model Watzon reads.
Three photo frames fanned out, the front one outlined in red.
A month grid with a red route running from the first day to a departure cell.
Two columns of line blocks, the changed lines on the right offset and filled red.
A transport network of connected nodes with the central hub in red.
A floor plan outline with its extruded copy behind it and one wall in red.
A decaying two-peak waveform above a run of keyboard blocks, one key in black.
Four tracks of sixteen steps with hits filled in, one snare hit in red.
Five clusters of six dots around a red centre, spread along an arc.
A ring of wedges of different lengths around a hollow centre, one wedge filled red.
Two grids of cells, the second shifted down a row so the newest column lines up empty.
A departures board grid with three rows called in red.
One long bar for the bill with a smaller red segment for the server's share.
A small block of world in isometric cubes, one raised block filled red.
A grid world with a red path stepping through it.
A box of photographs in perspective, one frame filled red.
